To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Cry1A (b) protein from transgenic maize can be detected by a biosensing device using specific antibody and peptide interaction.

(1) a theoretical three-dimensional structure of Cry1Ab protein was generated by homology modeling, (2) the selected model was refined by molecular dynamics simulations and its global structure was analyzed, (3) two immunoreactive peptides were identified, (4) the selected peptides were used to produce specific antibodies and (5) the antibodies were used for development of biosensing devices to be used for detection of Cry1A protein
the Cry1A (b) 16 protein from Bacillus thurigiensis has been successfully modeled, and the model was used to identify two immunoreactive peptides.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new biosensing devices based on Cry1A(b), as a marker of genetically modified maize, for use in food analysis.
the theoretical refinement of Cry1A (b) 16 toxin from B. thuringiensis, and the prediction of peptides as markers for the detection of genetically modified corn.
the identification of a protein Cry1A(b), a transgenic protein from genetically modified maize, and the production of specific antibodies to detect this protein in food samples.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Cry1A(b), a protein of Bacillus thuringiensi, has been successfully modeled, refined and analyzed.
we have developed a theoretical model of the Cry1Ab toxin from Bt and we have identified two peptides which can be used to detect this protein in transgenic maize.
Cry1A(b), a protein from Bacillus thurigiensis, was successfully modeled, and the molecular dynamics simulation allowed us to refine its three-dimensional structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we can use molecular modeling techniques for the theoretical refinement of the structure of the protein Cry1A(b), a protein from Bacillus thurningiensis that is used as a marker for the detection of transgenic crops, in this case, maize.

the use of molecular dynamics simulations can provide useful information about the three-dimensional structure of proteins, which can be used to design specific peptides as markers for detection of transgenic maize.
the Cry1A toxin is a promising candidate for use in biosensors to detect genetically modified organisms.
